title: Optional chaining (?.)
question: What does the optional chaining operator `?.` do in TypeScript/JavaScript?
searchIntent: what is optional chaining in typescript
realWorldScenario: `user?.address?.city` returns `undefined` instead of throwing if `user` or `address` is null/undefined.

title: Nullish coalescing (??)
question: What does the nullish coalescing operator `??` do and how is it different from `||`?
searchIntent: what is nullish coalescing operator typescript
realWorldScenario: `count ?? 0` returns `0` only if `count` is null/undefined; `||` would also trigger for `count = 0` or `count = ''` which are valid falsy values.

title: Optional function parameters
question: How do you define optional parameters in TypeScript functions and what is their default type?
searchIntent: how to define optional parameters typescript
realWorldScenario: `function greet(name: string, title?: string)` — `title` is `string | undefined` inside the function body.

title: Non-null assertion operator (!)
question: What is the non-null assertion operator `!` in TypeScript and when is it appropriate to use?
realWorldScenario: `document.getElementById('app')!` tells TypeScript you are certain the element exists and it won't be null.

title: strictNullChecks setting
question: What does `strictNullChecks: true` do in TypeScript and why should it always be enabled?
realWorldScenario: Without strictNullChecks, `null` and `undefined` silently inhabit every type, defeating much of TypeScript's safety.

title: Optional chaining with methods
question: Can you use optional chaining `?.` to call methods that might not exist on an object?
searchIntent: optional chaining with method call typescript
realWorldScenario: `user.getAddress?.()` calls the method only if it exists on the user object.
